transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I'm here because... well, I just keep blowing up at people. Over nothing, really. I work in retail, and the other day I yelled at one of my employees just for putting some stock on the wrong shelf. I mean, I really lost it. Afterward, I was literally shaking because... that’s just not how I usually treat people. It's like I have no fuse left.
Have you noticed that your emotions tend to swing suddenly or intensely, like feeling extremely anxious, sad, or empty in a short period, or having impulsive urges that you can't control?

No, not really. I don't think my emotions are swinging all over the place like that. I mean, I don't suddenly feel extremely sad or... or empty. And I definitely don't have impulsive urges to do things. 

It's honestly just the anger. Like I'm just walking around constantly on edge, and then I snap. But the other things you mentioned, no, I haven't experienced that.
When you have these angry outbursts, do you plan them ahead of time or do they just happen suddenly without thinking?

No, I definitely don't plan them. They just happen completely without thinking. Like with that employee I mentioned earlier—the one who put the stock on the wrong shelf. I didn't go into work intending to yell at him. I just blew up over nothing in a split second. 

I think that's why I was shaking so much afterward, because it just came out of nowhere and... well, like I said, that is just not how I usually treat people. It's completely sudden.

latest_inference.note: This turn ruled out impulsive urges and emotional swings, making Adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and disturbance of conduct and Disinhibited personality disorder less likely. The focus remains on sudden, unplanned anger outbursts, supporting Intermittent explosive disorder as the most likely diagnosis.
